runs: The archive that shows its work.

At a bank internship I built a parser for about {story.memos} legacy memos, and found there was no archive to run it on: the oldest records were only on paper, and loan applicants brought their earnings in notebooks that staff typed in by hand.

Archivist turns scanned financial archives into a verified database: every value is cited to its spot on the page, read twice with the second read blind, checked by arithmetic, and sent to a person when in doubt.

A value is accepted only when independent checks agree. No model grades its own work, and Archivist never changes a value: it proposes a correction with its evidence, and a person decides.

The pre-registered test on held-out pages of the Treasury Bulletin, which no model had seen: {real.cells} cells drawn in advance and labelled by the author from the printed page, never shown a model’s answer. Its one hypothesis, R1, said Archivist’s wrong values among those it accepts would be fewer than the single read’s, with the intervals apart. It was not met, in any variant. This is the official result, as scored.
